title: Erdogan and Putin Hold 90-Minute SCO Talks, Signal New Russian-Built Nuclear Plants; Ankara's Anti-Zionism Rhetoric Ignites Fresh Israel Clash
subhead: At the Bishkek SCO summit, Erdogan and Putin deepened energy and nuclear cooperation and Erdogan called ties 'at the most advanced level,' while a separate rhetorical war with Israel escalated after he branded Zionism 'genocidal.' Ankara also moved the Mecca defense pact toward institutionalization and raised its inflation forecast as the Iran war bites.

sections.heading: Erdogan-Putin SCO Talks: Nuclear Expansion and 'Privileged' Ties
sections.body: President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Vladimir Putin held 90-minute talks on the sidelines of the SCO summit in Bishkek, with Erdogan saying Türkiye-Russia ties are at 'the most advanced level' and Putin calling Türkiye a 'privileged partner,' according to Anadolu Agency and Daily Sabah. The two leaders discussed the Akkuyu nuclear plant and signaled steps toward new Russian-built nuclear projects, per Türkiye Today and AP News. Erdogan also said Türkiye will deepen cooperation with the Shanghai Cooperation Organization, which he hailed as a 'rising star,' while Ankara's official line stressed peaceful resolutions.
sections.whyItMatters: The nuclear expansion signals Türkiye is locking in long-term energy dependence on Russia even as it deepens ties with the SCO — a counterweight posture that sits awkwardly with its NATO membership and its parallel push into Western defense markets.

sections.heading: Erdogan's Anti-Zionism Remarks Spark New Israel-Turkey Clash
sections.body: A fresh rhetorical confrontation erupted after Erdogan called Zionism a 'genocidal ideology' and invoked the Holocaust in remarks against Israel, drawing a rebuke from Israel's Foreign Ministry, which branded the comments antisemitic, per The Jewish Chronicle and Ynetnews. Ankara hit back, with Turkish officials accusing Israel of 'genocide' and Erdogan warning of alleged Israeli 'sectarian' designs in the region while calling for the Iran war to end, according to Daily Sabah and The Times of Israel. The exchange follows weeks of military friction in Syria, where Israel struck an air base to block a Turkish deployment.
sections.whyItMatters: The escalation is now as much rhetorical as military — Erdogan is framing the rivalry as a civilizational confrontation over Zionism, which hardens the Israel-Turkey standoff and complicates any US-brokered de-escalation in Syria and the wider region.

sections.heading: Mecca Defense Pact Moves Toward Institutionalization in Istanbul
sections.body: Foreign ministers and top military chiefs of Türkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan met in Istanbul for the first session of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee created under the August 7 Mecca agreement, Al Jazeera reports. Turkish FM Hakan Fidan announced a secretariat in Riyadh and a Pakistani first secretary-general, and said the alliance remains 'open for the partnership and participation of any other country.' Officials said a roadmap is being prepared to expand the pact, with Bangladesh floated as a potential member, per Middle East Eye and DW. The meeting came as the US-Iran war resumed after a month-long lull.
sections.whyItMatters: The pact is moving from a political declaration — that an attack on one is an attack on all — toward an operational structure, giving Ankara a parallel security framework to NATO and the US umbrella at a moment of regional war.

sections.heading: Central Bank Holds Rate at 37%, Raises Inflation Forecast to 28%
sections.body: The Turkish central bank kept its policy rate unchanged at 37% and raised its end-2026 inflation forecast to 28% from 24%, citing war-driven energy costs, according to Turkish Minute, Daily Sabah and Hürriyet Daily News. Monthly inflation ran near 3%, keeping pressure on the bank, while Q2 GDP grew a less-than-forecast 2.3% as domestic demand shrank, Reuters reports. The bank vowed to maintain a tight stance even as it signaled a lower effective funding rate ahead, per ING analysis.
sections.whyItMatters: The Iran war is directly feeding Turkish inflation through energy prices, forcing the central bank to hold rates high and revise its forecast upward — a drag on growth that complicates Erdogan's economic reset just as the regional conflict shows no sign of ending.

sections.heading: Syria: Clashes in Aleppo as Kurdish Integration Deadline Looms
sections.body: Deadly clashes erupted between the Syrian army and the Kurdish-led SDF in Aleppo, killing at least two, as top Turkish officials visited Damascus ahead of a deadline for Kurdish integration into the Syrian state, Al Jazeera and NBC News report. Turkey's defense minister called planned elections by Syrian Kurds 'unacceptable,' and Erdogan signaled he plans his own visit to Syria, per Asharq Al-Awsat. Ankara has offered military aid to Damascus for counterterrorism, while the SDF's integration with the Syrian state remains stalled, Reuters notes.
sections.whyItMatters: The SDF-Damascus integration deal — a cornerstone of Ankara's post-Assad Syria policy — is fraying, and Turkey is pressing Damascus to deliver on Kurdish disarmament even as clashes risk pulling Ankara deeper into a new Syrian conflict.

sections.heading: Türkiye Joins NASA's Artemis Accords as 71st Signatory
sections.body: Türkiye signed NASA's Artemis Accords, becoming the 71st signatory nation, ahead of its first lunar mission, according to Daily Sabah and Türkiye Today. The move formalizes Ankara's participation in the US-led framework for lunar exploration and space cooperation, complementing its growing national space program.
sections.whyItMatters: The signing is a quiet but notable signal of Türkiye's hedging strategy — deepening space and technology cooperation with Washington even as it expands nuclear and security ties with Russia and the SCO.

bottomLine: Today's developments show Ankara running a deliberate multi-vector strategy: deepening nuclear and energy ties with Russia at the SCO while signing onto US-led space accords, institutionalizing a new defense pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, and escalating a rhetorical war with Israel even as the Iran conflict inflates its inflation forecast. The central bank's forecast hike to 28% is the clearest sign that the regional war is now the dominant constraint on Turkey's economy, while the Aleppo clashes warn that the SDF integration deadline could become the next flashpoint in Syria.
sources: Anadolu Agency, Daily Sabah, AP News, Türkiye Today, Al Jazeera, The Jewish Chronicle, Ynetnews, The Times of Israel, Middle East Eye, DW, Turkish Minute, Hürriyet Daily News, Reuters, ING, NBC News, Asharq Al-Awsat, The Washington Institute, NASA
